dossier.public_summary: The dip changes depth by more than a factor of two across TESS sectors and even within the same pipeline, individual transits vary widely, and there is a large phase-curve swing equal to the transit depth. The duration also implies a star density far too low for the target M dwarf. Together this is best explained by stellar variability or a blended binary rather than a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors (depth_change_pct 225.6, chi2 4556 dof 42) and within the same source (changes_within_a_source: QLP p 5.9e-09, SPOC 2-min p 9.3e-72, TESS-SPOC p 7.9e-245). A planet on target would be steady aside from aperture effects, not vary by factors of 2-3.
Individual transits are inconsistent, with outliers to 8522 ppm (sigma 7.7) and -4282 ppm (sigma -7.3), so the signal is not a repeatable planetary dip.
Large out-of-dip modulation equal to the transit depth on this period (spots or close binary) rather than flat phase curve expected for a planet.

Observed duration (1.996 h vs central_h 1.257 ratio 1.588) requires far lower stellar density than either TIC or Gaia radii allow, typical of a diluted or evolved star eclipse, not a planet on this M dwarf.
reasons.value: 18310 fit_log_density_ratio -1.905 duration ratio 1.588 (1.43 with Gaia radius)

reasons.why: Independent classifier trained on confirmed outcomes rates this as planet-like as only 7% of known planets, supporting the variability evidence.
